All 10 compounds are already baseline-resolved with substantial margin, so the clear optimization target is reducing analysis time. A much steeper full-range gradient should pull the late peak earlier while likely keeping the current minimum resolution comfortably above the threshold.

The 8 min gradient became too steep and compressed the critical mid-cluster around peaks 5–7, so a small increase in gradient time is the most direct way to recover resolution while staying near the fast optimum. Keeping the full-range endpoints and temperature fixed isolates the effect of gradient steepness.

The trend from 8 to 10 to 20 min shows the critical pair improves strongly as gradient time increases, and 10 min is likely still slightly too steep. Testing 12 min should better resolve the 5–7 cluster while remaining much faster than the original 20 min scout.

Resolution of the critical 6/7 pair is improving monotonically with gradient time, and the run is still comfortably in the no-time-penalty region. A 14 min gradient should continue that trend and may push the resolution term closer to 1 without sacrificing CRF to runtime.

The critical pair continues to open steadily with increasing gradient time, and there is still no time penalty at 14 min. Moving to 16 min is the most direct test for achieving full resolution scoring while likely remaining within the zero-penalty runtime region.

At 16 min the resolution term is maxed but a time penalty appears, so the optimum is likely near 14–16 min with slightly improved selectivity. Lowering temperature at 14 min is a targeted way to try to open the critical 6/7 pair enough to reach full resolution scoring while keeping runtime below the penalty threshold.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity and shifted the critical overlap to peaks 5/6, so the more promising direction is a modest increase in temperature at the best no-penalty gradient time. This tests whether higher temperature can improve the local selectivity around the compressed mid-cluster without lengthening the run.

Temperature changes both hurt the critical region, so keep 40 C and instead reduce the initial retention of the earliest peaks by raising phi0 slightly. This should redistribute gradient space toward the crowded mid-eluting cluster and may improve the limiting pair without adding runtime penalty.

Raising phi0 improved both runtime and the critical pair at 14 min, suggesting this endpoint better allocates gradient space. Extending to 16 min with the improved phi0 should test whether the resolution term can reach 1.000 while staying close to the optimum overall CRF.
